title: When the Trail Breaks
premise: Freya Pemberton, captain of the riverboat Kestrel, has run the Verrin River for twelve years, dodging grief and intimacy alike. When an earthquake lowers the tide and exposes a cave mouth the locals call the Door of Salt, she and her found family — deckhand Tomas, cartographer's widow Ines, and stowaway boy Pell — are swept into a current that drags them upstream toward the river's forbidden source, where a drowned mining town holds the truth about Freya's father's disappearance and a flood that will erase everything in forty-eight hours. Pursued by the Company men who want the cave's silver kept secret, Freya must choose between delivering Ines's evidence to the authorities downstream (her duty) and staying to pull Pell from the rising water (her heart). She chooses love, the family escapes as the source collapses, and the truth surfaces anyway — carried out on the flood they survived.
about_author: Rafael Delacroix is the pen name of a former barge hand who spent a decade working inland waterways before turning to fiction. Their adventure novels are praised for river-true detail and found-family warmth.

chapters.title: The Mood of the Water
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. A routine cargo run down the Verrin establishes the Kestrel's crew as a rough, loving family — Tomas's jokes, Ines's charts, Pell's stowaway hunger. Freya refuses a lucrative Company contract, revealing her distrust of authority. Emotional beat: comfort in routine, and the ache beneath it.

chapters.title: What the Tide Gave Back
chapters.summary: Pell's POV. An earthquake drains the river and reveals the Door of Salt, a cave the legends charge admission to. Pell sneaks in at dawn and finds a brass key stamped with the name Pemberton. Emotional beat: wonder curdling into dread when the tide turns and won't turn back.

chapters.title: Undertow
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. A freak current seizes the Kestrel and drags her through the cave mouth before she can drop anchor. The boat survives; the river behind them closes. Ines recognizes the cave markings as survey work — her dead husband's. Emotional beat: loss of control, the first bond of shared peril.

chapters.title: The Company's Men
chapters.summary: Tomas's POV. A Company skiff appears from a side channel; its leader, Corven, claims the river above is quarantined and demands they turn over 'salvage.' Tomas lies smoothly, but Corven marks the Kestrel. Emotional beat: loyalty tested — Tomas hides the brass key from Freya to protect Pell.

chapters.title: Ines's Charts
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. She deciphers her husband's final survey: the source hides the flooded town of Marrow Bend and proof the Company caused the dam failure that killed forty people, including Freya's father. Emotional beat: grief repurposed as purpose; love against duty as Ines weighs her widowhood against the truth.

chapters.title: Rapids at Nightfall
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. A night run through white water to outrun Corven; Tomas nearly drowns saving the wheel, and Freya realizes she loves him. They learn the source dam will fail in two days. Emotional beat: fear and tenderness braided together; the crew stops being passengers and becomes a crew.

chapters.title: Marrow Bend
chapters.summary: Pell's POV. They reach the drowned town and dive the steeple for Ines's husband's ledger. Pell finds the Pemberton name on the workers' roll — Freya's father died a whistleblower, not a deserter. Emotional beat: the past surfacing; Pell, orphaned, begins to believe in belonging.

chapters.title: Corven's Bargain
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. Corven corners them at the source: the ledger for safe passage downstream. Freya must trade her father's vindication for her family's lives. Tomas offers himself instead. Emotional beat: loyalty versus truth at its sharpest — Freya refuses the bargain.

chapters.title: The Source Gives Way
chapters.summary: Tomas's POV. The dam fails early. In the flood chaos Freya goes back for Pell against all sense, Tomas holds the Kestrel in the maelstrom, and Corven, shamed, throws them the towline that saves all three. Emotional beat: climax — love chosen over duty, and duty answered anyway.

chapters.title: Downstream
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. The flood delivers the ledger to every river town's doorstep; the Company falls, and Freya's father's name is cleared. The Kestrel runs the river again with the same crew, now openly a family. Emotional beat: quiet resolution — miles still measured, but now in years that matter.
